claims.claim: Egyptian pharaohs began collecting a twentieth of every grain harvest
claims.reason: Evidence map says 'typically around 20 percent' (a statistic), not that this was the established starting rate; script presents it as definitive

claims.claim: They called it a temporary emergency measure to fund pyramid construction
claims.reason: No evidence in the map supports the claim that Egyptians called taxation temporary or that it funded pyramid construction

claims.claim: it never went away
claims.reason: Editorial claim not supported by any evidence in the map

claims.claim: he came with a reed stick
claims.reason: No evidence in the map mentions sesh per hedj carrying a reed stick

claims.claim: Herodotus noted this without much surprise
claims.reason: Evidence map confirms Herodotus noted Persian improvement but says nothing about his emotional reaction or lack of surprise

claims.claim: Empires learned fast when money was at stake
claims.reason: Editorial generalization not supported by evidence map

claims.claim: They had conquered the territory, and they intended to profit from it
claims.reason: Attribution of intent not supported by evidence map

claims.claim: The word temporary did a lot of heavy lifting
claims.reason: Editorial commentary not supported by evidence map

claims.claim: They paid the state an agreed sum upfront, then extracted whatever they could from the local population. The margin was theirs.
claims.reason: Evidence map says publicani 'bid at auction for the right to collect taxes' but does not describe the upfront payment and margin extraction mechanism

claims.claim: That is a direct quote
claims.reason: Evidence map attributes the quote to Cicero's letters to Atticus, but the script omits this source attribution while still calling it a direct quote

claims.claim: Not their money. Their blood.
claims.reason: Script adds interpretive emphasis not present in the evidence map's version of the quote

claims.claim: The contractors had optimised themselves into a crisis
claims.reason: Modern framing/interpretation not supported by evidence map

claims.claim: He replaced the rapacious publicani with a permanent imperial bureaucracy
claims.reason: Evidence map says 'direct imperial officials' but does not describe it as a 'permanent imperial bureaucracy'

claims.claim: The language changed. The extraction did not. Something cleaner replaced something brutal, and the take remained.
claims.reason: Editorial interpretation not supported by evidence map

claims.claim: Viking raids had become unbearable
claims.reason: No evidence in the map describes the severity of Viking raids

claims.claim: King Ethelred needed money to buy peace
claims.reason: Evidence map does not attribute this motivation to King Aethelred

claims.claim: He levied the Danegeld, a tax on land, to raise silver for tribute
claims.reason: Evidence map confirms Danegeld was a land tax first levied in 991 CE but does not state it was specifically to raise silver for tribute

claims.claim: Temporary, of course. A crisis response.
claims.reason: No evidence in the map describes Danegeld as temporary or a crisis response

claims.claim: It had become a permanent line item in English fiscal life
claims.reason: No evidence in the map describes Danegeld becoming permanent

claims.claim: monetising the obligation to provide military service
claims.reason: Evidence map says scutage 'let knights pay cash instead of providing military service' but does not use the word 'monetising'

claims.claim: Emergency measure, permanent fixture, next generation inherits the bill
claims.reason: Pattern claim not supported by evidence map

claims.claim: The structure has not changed in five thousand years
claims.reason: Broad historical claim not supported by evidence map

claims.claim: A crisis arrives. The state needs money. It promises the measure is temporary. The crisis passes, the money stays, and the next crisis provides the template for the next temporary measure.
claims.reason: Generalized pattern claim not supported by evidence map

claims.claim: Egyptian officials beat farmers who could not pay
claims.reason: Evidence map says tomb reliefs depict officials beating farmers 'who fell behind' — script changes this to 'could not pay,' implying inability rather than delinquency

claims.claim: Roman collectors extracted blood from provincials
claims.reason: Treats Cicero's metaphorical quote as literal historical description

claims.claim: the Danegeld ate into English land until the silver ran out or the patience did
claims.reason: Poetic interpretation not supported by evidence map

claims.claim: Every time the system became so brutal that people chose revolt over compliance, revenue collapsed, and the state rebuilt it with better marketing
claims.reason: Sweeping generalization not supported by evidence map; only one example (Roman publicani) mentioned in evidence

claims.claim: Your grain, your silver, your attention. That is what they are asking for when they call something temporary.
claims.reason: Editorial commentary not supported by evidence map

claims.claim: The pharaohs needed your grain to build monuments to their own glory
claims.reason: Evidence map does not state grain taxes funded monuments or pharaohs' glory

claims.claim: The Romans needed your blood to sustain an empire that was never yours
claims.reason: Editorial interpretation mixing metaphorical quote with political commentary

claims.claim: The Danegeld needed your silver to fund wars you did not choose
claims.reason: Evidence map does not characterize Danegeld as funding wars; it describes it as tribute payment

claims.claim: Five thousand years of receipts say it will not be temporary
claims.reason: Concluding editorial claim not supported by evidence map
